dedupe_keys.name: predicted river erosion hazards to electricity transmission towers in the mersey valley under future flow scenarios 2018 2050 ukceh

description: This dataset from the NERC-funded project Erosion Hazards in River Catchments, by C. J. Feeney of UKCEH with University of Liverpool colleagues and D. Dodds of National Grid, predicts river erosion hazard to 40 electricity transmission towers along a reach of about 4.5 km of the Mersey valley in England. Historic channel change from 1976 to 2018 was digitised from Ordnance Survey maps and aerial imagery and used with Ashton Weir daily flows to calibrate the CAESAR-Lisflood landscape evolution model on a 15 m DEM. The two best calibrations were then run for 2018 to 2050 under six hypothetical flow scenarios, a baseline repeating the previous 32 years and daily flows raised by 10 to 50 percent, and landscape change was extracted at each tower to rank erosion risk. The dataset includes the model input files so runs can be repeated, results as shapefiles and CSV, and R code to reproduce most analyses; it is available for free download under the Open Government Licence. Coverage is one Mersey valley reach. Caveats: the authors stress that channel change is chaotic and the flow scenarios are hypothetical scalings of past flows. Simulation uses are tower-level geomorphic hazard for transmission asset exposure and adaptation planning. Related records: case_study-national-grid-substation-flood-defence-framework covers National Grid flood adaptation.
